subject: Follow-up: performance targets, streaming behavior, and geo-control constraints
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Green <sophie.green@acmemedia.com>; Rajiv Menon <rajiv.menon@acmemedia.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 13 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: performance targets, streaming behavior, and geo-control constraints

Hi Sophie / Rajiv —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap of the performance items we discussed and a proposed next-step checklist so we can size a pilot: 

1) Targets you stated
   - P95 generation latency target: <= 150ms for 512-token responses (US region)
   - P99 target: <= 350ms for the same SLA
   - Streaming: client expects token-level streaming with end-to-end average gap <= 30ms between tokens for interactive flows

2) Throughput & concurrency
   - Typical baseline: 20 concurrent interactive sessions during peak; burst up to 150 concurrency for short spikes (5–10m)
   - Bulk embedding throughput: roughly 600 docs/hr in batch windows (can be async)

3) Regional constraints
   - Primary routing preference: US for global users; failover to EU for certain EU-origin traffic
   - Data residency: EU customer subset must keep request logs and payloads in EU region only; no automatic replication to US control plane without consent

4) Security / compliance notes
   - You requested KMS integration + audit log retention (rolling 13 months) on EU data buckets

Next steps (proposal):
   - We’ll provide a short performance-runbook (attached) with recommended instance types and batching config.
   - Please share the traffic matrix for your Madison feed (I attached a CSV placeholder) so we can model concurrency/peak shape.
   - Ops check: confirm whether EU-only residency applies to embeddings as well as generation requests.

Soojin (cc’d) will propose a minimal pilot — 2 weeks of dedicated capacity for the interactive flow, with a short smoke test to validate streaming latency targets. If that looks good, Ben can scope pricing/discount for the pilot.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a calendar invite for a 30-min pilot kickoff once we get the traffic matrix and the residency confirmation.

Best,
Mateo
Mateo Alvarez
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
attachments: redwood-performance-guidance.pdf (attachment stub), acme-traffic-matrix.csv (attachment stub)

From: Sophie Green <sophie.green@acmemedia.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rajiv Menon <rajiv.menon@acmemedia.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Jun 2026 10:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: performance targets, streaming behavior, and geo-control constraints

Thanks Mateo — really helpful summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- P95/P99: the 150ms/350ms numbers are for our interactive editor (users typing prompts, short responses). For long-form generation (1k+ tokens) we can accept higher latency (up to 2s p95).
- Streaming: the 30ms token gap is ideal — can you confirm whether that assumes the model runs on a single GPU per request (no cross-host hops)?
- EU residency: yes, embeddings and request payloads for EU customers must remain in EU. Logs we can discuss (some logs can be anonymized) — will confirm by EOD Monday.

One more ask: can you show a simple failure-mode for multi-region routing? For example, if EU region is overloaded, do we redirect to US and still keep EU data bounded? We need to understand acceptable trade-offs for our compliance team.

Thanks — Sophie
Senior Product Manager, Acme Media

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Green <sophie.green@acmemedia.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: performance targets, streaming behavior, and geo-control constraints

Sophie — great questions. Short answers below, and I’ll add the technical notes to the runbook this morning.

- Streaming token gap: the 30ms assumption is for a single-host execution where the model and runtime stream directly from the token generator to the client (no cross-host KV fetches). In multi-host sharded setups token gaps commonly increase; we’ll include an optimized single-shard config for the pilot.

- Failure-mode / routing: we can configure strict residency with these options:
   a) Strict EU-only: requests originating from EU go to EU endpoints; if EU is at capacity we can queue/spill to warm standby capacity inside EU (preferred for compliance).
   b) EU with consented failover: if EU capacity exhausted, route to US but drop any payloads flagged as residency-sensitive (or use on-the-fly anonymization). This requires explicit written consent and a documented fall-back playbook for your compliance team.

For the pilot I recommend option (a) — start strict, then evaluate consented failover for non-sensitive traffic.

Action items I’m taking now:
  - Update the runbook with single-shard streaming config and expected token-gap numbers.
  - Draft a short failover playbook (flowchart + ops checklist) and share via Drive link.
  - Ben to send pilot pricing and an optional add-on for EU-dedicated capacity.

Can you confirm: 1) EU residency applies to embeddings as well, and 2) whether your compliance team needs any extra metadata redaction for logs?

Cheers,
Mateo

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Green <sophie.green@acmemedia.com>, Rajiv Menon <rajiv.menon@acmemedia.com>
Cc: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: performance targets, streaming behavior, and geo-control constraints

Hi Sophie / Rajiv —

Following Mateo’s proposal on the pilot and pricing:

- Pilot scope (2 weeks): dedicated capacity for interactive editor flow, single-shard model for streaming validation, metrics collection for p95/p99, and a short embedding batch test.
- Pilot price (discounted): $9,500 for a two-week reserved pool (includes 2 hours of engineering support/week). Add-on: EU-dedicated capacity option +$3,000 for the pilot period.
- Contract: we’ll issue a short SOW and an offer via DocuSign. If you want the EU-strict setup permanently, that will become a line item in the Dedicated capacity contract.

Next steps for us:
  1) Sophie / Rajiv to confirm residency applies to embeddings and whether logs need extra redaction (reply by EOD Tues).
  2) If yes, I’ll push the pricing + SOW with the EU add-on and DocuSign link.
  3) Mateo to set pilot kickoff calendar once we receive the traffic CSV.

DocuSign link (will be sent once we have your confirmation): https://docusign.example.com/ACME-987654

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
